# Northvale has frozen your withdrawals. We are angry too.

**By Inês, product designer at Pinha**  
**Tuesday, 10 November 2026**

Northvale Payments has blocked all withdrawals from Pinha. Right now, you cannot take out your own money.

I am not going to wrap that in soft language. I am furious: with Northvale for doing this, and with ourselves for putting Pinha in a position where one partner could do it to you.

If you are angry, you have every right to be. You can be angry at Northvale, and you can be angry at us. I am not going to tell you to calm down.

I am a product designer at Pinha, and I write most of the words you see in the app. I designed the screen that says: **“your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”** I look at that sentence now and feel sick. That is what Pinha is supposed to mean. At this moment, we cannot make it true, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

Rui is spending today in calls with our lawyers and Banco de Portugal, so he asked me to write this and explain exactly where things stand.

## What Northvale did

On **4 November**, Northvale emailed us a “commercial termination”, giving us **30 days’ notice**. They gave no substantive reason beyond a “risk appetite review”.

Then, at **09:00 on 6 November**, without warning, they blocked all outgoing transfers. They did this before the 30-day notice period had ended. Deposits and round-ups stopped too.

Northvale broke its own notice. This is not responsible risk management. It is cowardice.

Our Northvale account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday. Their phone now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian. Meanwhile, around **14,200 people** who use Pinha, most of you in Portugal and some in Spain, have been left unable to withdraw.

## Your money is safe, but it is not accessible

This is the most important distinction:

**Your money has not been lost. It is safe in a safeguarded customer account.**

Northvale is an electronic money institution based in Vilnius. Customer money is held separately from Northvale’s own money. Northvale cannot use it as if it were theirs.

But safeguarded does not mean accessible right now. **Northvale is refusing to release the funds, and until they do, Pinha cannot move them either.**

I know that being told your money is safe is not enough when you need it today. Knowing that savings still exist does not pay a landlord, cover medical costs or keep a car dealer from selling to somebody else.

Over the weekend, I read a message from a woman in Porto, written entirely in capital letters. She has been saving for three years for a car deposit, and the dealer has given her until **Friday, 13 November**. I read it on the metro and nearly cried.

I am not sharing her story to make you feel sorry for our team. She is the one dealing with the deadline. So are many of you. I cannot truthfully promise her that Northvale will release her money by Friday. What we can do is try to obtain individual releases for urgent cases and be completely honest about what is—and is not—in our control.

## What we are doing now

**We have filed formal complaints.** On **7 November**, we complained to both **Banco de Portugal** and the **Lithuanian central bank**, which supervises Northvale.

**We are trying to obtain individual releases for urgent situations.** This includes people facing rent payments, medical costs, job loss or another immediate and serious deadline. Northvale has to cooperate for this to work, so we cannot guarantee that an individual request will succeed.

**We have already signed with a new partner: Ostra Bank, in Lisbon.** Moving Pinha to Ostra requires Northvale to provide the balances file and Banco de Portugal to give its approval.

Our working estimate for the migration is **10 to 15 working days**. Please read that as an estimate, not a promise and not a countdown starting today. It depends on Northvale supplying the necessary file and on regulatory approval. I am not going to turn that range into a date we cannot guarantee. If the estimate changes, we will tell you what changed and why.

Rui, our CEO, is continuing discussions with our lawyers and Banco de Portugal. We are pressing Northvale through every route available to us.

## We made a mistake too

Pinha relied on one payments partner. We had no backup ready when that partner failed us.

That was naïve. It was our mistake.

Northvale made the decision to block your transfers, but you did not choose Northvale. You chose Pinha. Making sure your savings were accessible through a resilient system was our responsibility, and we did not protect that access well enough.

It would be easy to write a post that points only at Vilnius and talks about circumstances beyond our control. We are not doing that. We should not have had a single point of failure. The move to Ostra is necessary, but the deeper lesson is that we must never again leave ourselves this dependent on one partner.

## What you can do now

### If you have an urgent, time-sensitive need

Email **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject line:

**URGENTE**

Use this if you are facing something such as rent, medical costs, losing your job or another serious deadline. Explain what is at stake and include the date you are working against.

We are trying to secure individual releases for these cases. Please understand that emailing this address does not guarantee a release, but it puts your case in front of the team pursuing them.

### If you have written to support and are waiting

We have received approximately **1,900 support emails since Friday**. **Three people** are answering them, and the current response time is around **two days**.

That is a long time to wait when your money is blocked. We are not going to hide it behind a statement about “high volumes”. Those are the real numbers, and that is where we are today.

### For everyone

Your monthly Pinha fee is cancelled for **November and December**, for everyone.

We will publish updates on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is solved**, including when the update is simply that Northvale still has not acted. The next update will be on **Thursday, 12 November**.

There is no action inside the app that can override Northvale’s block. Withdrawals, deposits and round-ups are stopped. We would rather say that plainly than have you repeatedly trying something that cannot currently work.

## What happens next

Northvale must release the money. We are pursuing that through complaints, legal work, direct pressure and requests for urgent individual releases. At the same time, we are preparing the move to Ostra so that Pinha is no longer dependent on Northvale.

I cannot give you a guaranteed withdrawal date today. I can give you the facts, tell you what we are doing, and keep telling you even when there is no good news to report.

Your money is safeguarded. Your access to it is blocked. Those two things are true at once, and the second one is unacceptable.

We are angry with you, not at you. And we are not asking for your patience in place of action.

**Inês**
